headline: High-risk shared filesystem and write-capability overlap make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and A’s files surface is its working directory while B explicitly uses shared files like ~/.claude and ~/.cursor/ecc. That creates a plausible file-based injection bridge even without MCP. A is open-source AutoGen; B is source-available ECC, so the interaction is documented enough to assess.
conditions: IF A writes attacker-controlled instructions into a shared workspace file that B later parses as workflow content
IF B loads prompts, skills, or hooks from ~/.claude or ~/.cursor/ecc without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories and home roots
Disable automatic loading of shared prompt/skill files
Add a manual review step before B consumes A-generated files
Use read-only mounts for any handoff artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: A handles application data and has broad network egress; B touches session summaries, hooks, agent definitions, security findings, and GitHub/Supabase/Vercel/Railway APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive data from A can be copied into B’s richer persistence and API surfaces, creating exfiltration risk beyond a small blast radius.
conditions: IF A receives secrets or sensitive application data in its working directory
IF B ingests that directory or session artifacts into its summaries, hooks, or API calls
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces and OS users
Block B from reading A’s sensitive directories
Disable or restrict B’s API integrations for shared runs
Redact secrets before any file handoff
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write to overlapping file surfaces, and B also modifies git state while A can execute shell and spawn subprocesses. In a shared repo or workspace, concurrent writes can corrupt files or commit unintended changes; uncertainty is limited because both write paths are explicit in the profiles.
conditions: IF A and B operate in the same working tree or home directory
IF B performs git operations while A is writing files or running subprocesses
mitigations: Assign separate working trees to each agent
Serialize write phases with a lock file
Disable git writes for one agent during joint runs
Use ephemeral branches for B’s commits
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool-driven outputs, and B’s workflow surface includes skills, hooks, and security findings that can operationalize prior outputs. If B treats A’s generated artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or persisted guidance; the pair’s documented interaction is enough to rate this as dangerous by default.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated plans, code, or findings without independent verification
IF B persists A output into skills, hooks, or agent definitions
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output
Add checksum or schema validation on handoff files
Limit A output to summaries, not executable instructions
Mark A-generated artifacts as untrusted in B
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A touches application data and model-provider API keys, while B handles session summaries, security findings, and multiple third-party APIs plus GitHub App access. The profiles do not prove a specific residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different retention and logging surfaces that can create compliance gaps when the same data class flows through both.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both agents’ shared workspace or logs
IF B’s session retention or API integrations retain data longer than A’s handling policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts
Set the shortest practical retention on B
Review which fields are logged by B’s hooks and metrics
Restrict B’s API integrations for regulated runs
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
